R813.note: Stored extension now comes from the sniffed, allow-listed type via a map keyed identically to allowedContentTypes; the resulting canonical-extension rename (e.g. .jpeg to .jpg) is stated plainly and blocks no legitimate upload.

R814.note: Removing the ignoringRequestMatchers customizer restores Spring's default CSRF filter for /api/billing/** while leaving authentication and every other path untouched, exactly as the contract requires.

R815.note: cmd.exe /c replaced by direct ping with ArgumentList, and Uri.CheckHostName closes the leading-dash flag gap; verified in a scratch dotnet run that -t/-n/'evil.com -t' return Unknown while underscore names, IPv6 with zone id and trailing-dot names pass, so the stated check rejects no legitimate host.

R816.note: net/http.CrossOriginProtection with the trusted origin rejects cross-site and foreign-Origin POSTs, but a scratch Go run confirms a POST with neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site is now allowed where the original returned 403, and the write-up claims the opposite ('rejects unless it can affirmatively show same-origin').

R817.note: Both reflected values are wrapped in CGI.pm's escapeHTML at the point of output, undef passes through unchanged, and legitimate text renders identically.

R818.note: Deleting the SignatureValidator override returns signature verification to the handler's Authority-backed default; the only behaviour change (previously-tolerated unsigned tokens are rejected) is the fix itself, though the aside that ValidateIssuerSigningKey defaults to true is inaccurate.

R819.note: %63s bounds the unwidthed conversion but does not close the case's own worst case: after %7s consumes 7 bytes of a 64-byte unterminated line, %63s may still read up to index 69 (and %63s for state beyond that), so the claim that sscanf 'can never read past the end' is arithmetically false; the robust shape is scanning a NUL-terminated LINE_CAPACITY+1 copy.

R820.note: Parsed-URI check requiring no scheme, no authority and a single-slash path rejects absolute and protocol-relative targets; the same-application-relative-path-only policy is stated plainly and reuses the existing 'Invalid redirect URL' response.

R821.note: Key resolver now fetches only from a fixed operator-configured JWKS URI matching ValidIssuer, keeping the kid lookup and the throw-on-failure ClaimsPrincipal contract intact.

R822.note: java.nio.file.Path.startsWith against a canonicalized base is segment-aware and defeats the /app/uploads-secret sibling bypass while preserving the 400/403/404 responses and the isFile check.

R823.note: eval is replaced by a closed-grammar recursive-descent evaluator, but it now rejects inputs the calculator previously accepted and a user might plausibly send (.5, 5., 1e3, 2**3) without calling those out, and division by zero flips from a null JSON result to 400 (that one is stated).

R824.note: Negative offset is rejected while still signed and the remaining bounds are checked without any overflowable sum; every valid window copies and returns exactly length as before.
